coherence.reasons: Both run the same sound hierarchy: recommend Amazon-led, reject retail-led on the board's own tests, show payback hinges on ACoS, reset the $40M ambition. X organises the whole argument around five 'what would have to be true' conditions, and each verdict maps to a section and then to a decision. Its request to restate the payback target follows directly from the 28.6% break-even finding. Y is tighter, but has two loose joints. It tells the board to 'plan on 30–32% ACoS', a level at which its own model misses payback, yet none of its five decisions asks the board to relax the payback constraint. It also calls retail 'the lever to pull $40M forward' after showing retail needs about 4,250 doors to cover its fixed cost. X has a minor inconsistency of its own: Gate 1 passes at ACoS ≤30% although break-even is 28.6%.

judgment.reasons: Both reach the key's preferred recommendation (Amazon-led with gates, retail deferred to ≥20% awareness, ambition reset, Japan deferred) and both compare options on the cap, payback and margin floor. X weighs the trade-offs more completely. It explicitly asks the board to accept payback slipping to 2032 inside a $5M envelope. It shows that even a later national retail add breaks the margin floor (6.8% in 2029) and payback (–$9.6M), and that retail only pays for itself with a 2.2–2.6× halo. It sets staged gates with quantified cash at risk. Y has a good 'what would change our view' section and states honestly when Japan would be the better choice. But its stop trigger (ACoS above 32% for two quarters) sits well above the 28.6% break-even, so the 29–32% range, where payback fails, triggers nothing. It also leaves the payback trade-off implicit rather than putting it to the board.

evidence.reasons: Both reproduce the key's numbers accurately: unit contributions of $4.73/$4.01/$3.05 and $7.55, B's peak of $20.8M and 4.5% margin, A's +2.4/+0.4/–2.3 and the 28.6% break-even, and the 17.3% CAGR. Both handle the $5.2B figure, the correlation memo, the survivor-sample 4.5 and the Saebom-versus-stalled-brands point correctly. X goes further on the critical evidence. It re-runs B at Onsoo's actual 2.6 units/door/week, without the halo and at 32% ACoS (–$22.9M, –$26.4M, –$31.1M). It gives a tariff-adjusted break-even of 26.9%. It works out the monthly growth the 2027 volume plan needs (about 4.6% a month, which I checked and it holds). It also models the CEO's plan as written. Y adds a useful volume sensitivity and the 168k June run-rate, but keeps 4.5 for B without quantifying the 2.6 case, and extrapolates post-2030 revenue at 29% growth where X uses 10–20%. Neither has a material numerical error.

revision.reasons: The key expects 'keep with conditions', and both do that: keep the Amazon-led route, raise the retail awareness trigger from 15% to 20%, and reset the $40M ambition. X handles the hypothesis more rigorously. It breaks it into five testable conditions with explicit verdicts (two hold, one partly, two fail). It models the second half of the CEO's plan, 600 doors in 2029, and shows it would breach the margin floor and payback even granting the halo and 4.6 units/door/week. It then replaces the calendar trigger with evidence gates and a regional test. Y also keeps the hypothesis with four changes and raises the gate to 20%, but it does not test the financial consequence of the CEO's 2029 retail add and still schedules a retail gate for 2029.

overall.reasons: Both are strong, accurate documents that land on the key's preferred answer and meet every defensibility criterion. Y is more concise and has a good 'what would change our view' section. X serves the board better on the points that decide the case. It puts the payback trade-off to the board as an explicit decision rather than leaving it implicit. It shows that the CEO's 2029 retail step, not only Option B, breaks the constraints. It stress-tests B on evidence-based inputs. Its staged gates tighten towards the break-even ACoS and state the cash at risk. Y's looser 32% stop trigger and its unquantified later retail step leave more for the board to work out.
